beats.text: A model forgets everything between calls.
beats.say: A language model forgets everything between calls. All an agent remembers is whatever you put in its context window.
Short-term memory is the context window: the instructions, the conversation, and the tool results. It is fast, but limited in size.
When it fills up, you have to trim, or summarize the older messages, or the agent loses the start of its task.

beats.text: Long-term memory lives outside the model.
beats.say: Long-term memory lives outside the model, in a database or vector store. The agent saves facts there, and retrieves the relevant ones when needed.
Useful kinds of memory: facts about the user, past episodes of what worked, and procedures for how to do tasks.
But more memory isn't always better. Wrong or stale memories can mislead the agent. Decide what to save, and when to forget.
